html:
A Nigerian novelist, poet and critic, often called the father of modern African literature. He was born into an Igbo Christian family in the town of Ogidi in Nigeria.

His first novel, Things Fall Apart (1958), tells of Okonkwo, a proud man in an Igbo village, whose world is broken by the coming of missionaries and British rule. It showed Igbo society as complex and whole, against the European picture of Africa without history, and it became the most widely read African novel, translated into dozens of languages. Novels about later times followed, such as No Longer at Ease and Arrow of God.

As founding editor of Heinemann's African Writers Series he helped launch a generation of writers. His 1975 lecture attacked Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness as racist and changed how the book is taught.

During the Nigerian Civil War he worked for Biafra's government. After a car crash in 1990 left him in a wheelchair, he taught in the United States. Writers such as Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie count him as their model.
sum: A Nigerian novelist, poet and critic, often called the father of modern African literature. He was born into an Igbo Christian family in the town of Ogidi in Nigeria.
